events.title: Hispanic Heritage Month 2026
events.description:
Hispanic Heritage Month 2026
“Unidos Somos Más — Together We Are More!”

Join the Stony Brook University community as we celebrate 37 years of Hispanic Heritage Month at SBU!

From September 15 through November 6, we invite students, faculty, staff, departments, student organizations, and community partners to celebrate the rich cultures, histories, identities, achievements, and contributions of Latine communities.

This year’s theme, “Unidos Somos Más — Together We Are More!”, reflects the strength and possibilities that emerge when we come together, share our stories, celebrate our wide range of identities, and build meaningful connections. The Hispanic Heritage Month Committee, DICE, and campus partners will offer a variety of cultural, educational, social, and community-building programs for the Stony Brook community.

Whether you are a department, student organization, faculty or staff member, or community partner, we invite you to take part in HHM 2026. Attend a signature event, support a student organization, learn something new, share your culture, or host an event or initiative of your own. Every contribution helps make Hispanic Heritage Month a more vibrant and inclusive reflection of our community.

Whether through the arts, music and food, cultural traditions, meaningful dialogue, educational programs, academic/research opportunities, career networking, awards and scholarships, civic engagement, or simply connecting, there are many ways to celebrate, participate, and be part of HHM. 

For event details and the full Hispanic Heritage Month 2026 calendar, visit www.stonybrook.edu/hhm.

Because when we come together, Unidos Somos Más — Together We Are More!

events.title: Shape the future of ECO-AI
events.description:
Love tech? Passionate about the planet? Let’s shape something really that Matters! 

The Center for Earth and Environmental Science (C4E) is hosting a super exciting guest talk, and we want YOU there!

November 4th at 12:30 PM, Dr. Raju Rajan, Director of ReWild Long Island just scored an awesome grant to build an AI-powered Landcare Information Hub dedicated to Long Island native plants, composting, and sustainable living. ReWild already has crews of SBU interns and volunteers making waves, and now they are looking for the next wave of student powerhouses to help shape, code, and guide this app responsibly.

There’s a spot for you to get real-world, hands-on experience:
Content Squad: Love nature or speak Spanish? Help write and vet localized, smart guides on native gardening and composting. Multilingual students with Spanish skills are highly needed to build authentic, culturally nuanced content.
Policy: How do we make sure AI actually does good? Help build frameworks to measure the app's real-world impact and figure out what actually motivates neighbors to go green.
Tech Builders: Want to build a green AI machine? Help design a community-scale architecture that is low on carbon footprint but high on impact, so it's easy for a small nonprofit to run.

Ready to make a real impact on Long Island?

 Scan the QR code and come to the talk on November 4th to see how you can get involved!

Can't make it? No worries! Reach out directly to Dr. Rajan at raju@rewildlongisland.org to pitch in. See you there!

events.title: SEAM Movie Day!
events.description:
SEAM Movie Day is a film screening and social event hosted by South East Asian Made (SEAM), where students will have the opportunity to relax, enjoy a movie together, and connect with others in a welcoming environment. The event aims to bring students from different backgrounds together through a shared entertainment experience while promoting community building, cultural appreciation, and social interaction.

At the beginning of the event, participants will be welcomed and given a brief introduction to SEAM, its mission, and the selected film. The introduction will highlight the importance of creating an inclusive space where students can connect through shared interests and experiences.

Participants will then enjoy a screening of the selected movie in SAC Ballroom B. The screening will provide students with an opportunity to take a break from their academic responsibilities, relax, and enjoy an entertaining experience alongside their peers.

Following the screening, participants will have the opportunity to socialize, share their thoughts about the movie, and connect with other attendees. This will encourage conversations and help strengthen connections within the Stony Brook community.

The event will take place on November 1, 2026, from 3:30 PM to 5:30 PM in SAC Ballroom B. SEAM's executive board members will assist with event setup, welcoming attendees, coordinating the screening, and cleaning up afterward.

By providing a relaxed and welcoming environment, SEAM Movie Day supports SEAM's mission of fostering an inclusive community and bringing students together through shared experiences. The event encourages students to build friendships, engage with others, and strengthen their sense of belonging on campus.

events.title: Día de Los Muertos | Day of the Dead Celebration
events.description:
Día de los Muertos | Day of the Dead Celebration
Date: Monday, November 2nd, 2026
Time: 12:30-1:45 PM
Location: Latin American & Caribbean Studies Center- Social and Behavioral Sciences Building, Room N335

Join us as we honor and celebrate Día de Los Muertos (Day of the Dead) — a vibrant cultural tradition that pays tribute to the lives and memories of our loved ones who have passed. Although Día de los Muertos is celebrated throughout Latin America, it has deep pre-colonial indigenous roots.

Guests are invited to contribute photos or small offerings to a community ofrenda (altar) in remembrance of family, friends, and historical/cultural icons who have inspired them. Honor and celebrate your departed loved ones (human and animal) over lunch, marigolds, Spanish poetry, and mingling at our altar! Tacos and pan provided

Enjoy Latin American refreshments as we come together to celebrate life, legacy, and cultural tradition. 

This event is free and open to all.

Sponsored by:
Hispanic Heritage Month Committee
Diversity, Intercultural and Community Engagement (DICE)
Latin American and Caribbean Studies Center (LACS)
Department of Hispanic Languages and Literature (HLL)

events.description:
The University Affairs Committee serves as a space for undergraduate students to raise concerns, discuss campus-wide issues, and work on initiatives that improve the student experience at Stony Brook University. Led by the Vice President of University Affairs, the committee focuses on areas such as academic policies, accessibility, transportation and parking, campus technology, student services, and other university-wide concerns.

Committee members work together to gather student feedback, develop advocacy initiatives, research potential policy solutions, and communicate student concerns to university administrators and shared governance bodies. The committee also helps strengthen undergraduate representation within University governance and provides students with an opportunity to become directly involved in creating positive change on campus.

All undergraduate students are welcome to attend, share concerns, propose ideas, and get involved in University Affairs initiatives.

events.title: USG Club Co-Lab: Performance Clubs
events.description:
USG x SEA Club Co-Lab Series

USG and Student Engagement & Activities invite club leaders to the Club Co-Lab Series, a set of collaborative working sessions organized by club category. Each Co-Lab is designed to help organizations meet relevant partners, share resources, develop joint-event ideas, and leave with practical next steps for collaboration.

Each session will include networking, an icebreaker, a brief USG presentation on funding, treasury information, the Club Closet, and important SEA guidelines, followed by a department-specific resource presentation and interactive collaboration activities. Clubs will take part in activities such as Resources Bingo, scenario planning, and a “Build Your Own Event” challenge that helps them identify potential partners and turn an idea into a feasible program.

USG will also collect feedback and follow up on collaboration commitments so that these conversations lead to real partnerships, shared programming, and stronger support for clubs throughout the year. Attendees will have the opportunity to win snacks and gift-card incentives.

We strongly encourage each organization to send at least two representatives, ideally members of the club’s Core Four: President, Vice President, Secretary, and Treasurer.

Club Co-Lab Schedule

September 14: Sports Clubs
September 16: Academic and Honor Societies
September 28: Cultural Organizations
September 30: Activism and Advocacy Organizations
October 19: Religious and Spiritual Organizations
October 21: Leisure Activities Organizations
October 28: Community Awareness and Service Organizations
November 4: Performance Clubs
November 10: Media Organizations

Unless otherwise indicated on the individual event page, sessions will be held in Student Activities Center (SAC) 302. Please attend the session that best fits your organization’s primary category.

events.title: The Beer Goggles Challenge
events.description:
The Beer Goggles Challenge is an activity designed to simulate the effects of alcohol impairment. Participants wear specially designed goggles that distort vision and coordination, mimicking the sensation of being intoxicated. During the challenge, students attempt simple tasks like walking in a straight line, picking up objects, or navigating obstacles. The goal is to demonstrate how alcohol impairs judgment, reaction time, and motor skills, reinforcing the dangers of driving under the influence or engaging in risky behaviors while intoxicated. It provides a hands-on, impactful learning experience about the real-world consequences of alcohol impairment.

events.title: Cambodian Krama Scarf Painting Night
events.description:
Cambodian Krama: Scarf Painting Night is a guided cultural arts and crafts workshop centered around the krama, a traditional Cambodian checkered scarf that is an important part of everyday life and cultural identity in Cambodia. Rather than simply recreating the appearance of the textile, the event will introduce students to the krama’s history, recognizable patterns, cultural significance, and the many ways it is traditionally worn and used. At the beginning of the event, participants will receive a brief introduction to the history and cultural significance of the Cambodian krama. Students will learn about its recognizable checkered design and its versatility in Cambodian daily life, including its use as a scarf, head covering, sun protection, and practical everyday cloth. Participants will then be introduced to traditional krama patterns and colors as inspiration for their own designs. Examples will be provided so students can understand the visual characteristics of the textile before beginning the activity. Each participant will receive a plain scarf and fabric painting materials to create their own krama-inspired scarf. Students will be encouraged to experiment with checkered patterns, repetition, symmetry, and color while still having the freedom to personalize their designs. All scarves, fabric paints, painting supplies, protective table coverings, and cleanup materials will be provided for up to 50 participants, so no previous artistic experience or personal materials are required. By combining a cultural introduction with a hands-on textile activity, the event allows students to learn about Cambodian heritage in an interactive and memorable way. Participants will leave with both a personally designed scarf and a greater understanding of the krama and its place within Cambodian culture and everyday life.

events.title: University Affairs Committee Meeting
events.description:
The University Affairs Committee serves as a space for undergraduate students to raise concerns, discuss campus-wide issues, and work on initiatives that improve the student experience at Stony Brook University. Led by the Vice President of University Affairs, the committee focuses on areas such as academic policies, accessibility, transportation and parking, campus technology, student services, and other university-wide concerns.

Committee members work together to gather student feedback, develop advocacy initiatives, research potential policy solutions, and communicate student concerns to university administrators and shared governance bodies. The committee also helps strengthen undergraduate representation within University governance and provides students with an opportunity to become directly involved in creating positive change on campus.

All undergraduate students are welcome to attend, share concerns, propose ideas, and get involved in University Affairs initiatives.

events.title: USG Club Co-Lab: Media Organizations
events.description:
USG x SEA Club Co-Lab Series

USG and Student Engagement & Activities invite club leaders to the Club Co-Lab Series, a set of collaborative working sessions organized by club category. Each Co-Lab is designed to help organizations meet relevant partners, share resources, develop joint-event ideas, and leave with practical next steps for collaboration.

Each session will include networking, an icebreaker, a brief USG presentation on funding, treasury information, the Club Closet, and important SEA guidelines, followed by a department-specific resource presentation and interactive collaboration activities. Clubs will take part in activities such as Resources Bingo, scenario planning, and a “Build Your Own Event” challenge that helps them identify potential partners and turn an idea into a feasible program.

USG will also collect feedback and follow up on collaboration commitments so that these conversations lead to real partnerships, shared programming, and stronger support for clubs throughout the year. Attendees will have the opportunity to win snacks and gift-card incentives.

We strongly encourage each organization to send at least two representatives, ideally members of the club’s Core Four: President, Vice President, Secretary, and Treasurer.

Club Co-Lab Schedule

September 14: Sports Clubs
September 16: Academic and Honor Societies
September 28: Cultural Organizations
September 30: Activism and Advocacy Organizations
October 19: Religious and Spiritual Organizations
October 21: Leisure Activities Organizations
October 28: Community Awareness and Service Organizations
November 4: Performance Clubs
November 10: Media Organizations

Unless otherwise indicated on the individual event page, sessions will be held in Student Activities Center (SAC) 302. Please attend the session that best fits your organization’s primary category.
Dress Code: Casual (jeans ok)
---

events.title: NMDP x SBU Biweekly Tabling
events.description:
NMDP x SBU is the stony brook chapter of NMDP, an international non-profit dedicated to supporting blood stem cell donation. Blood stem cell donation is a curative treatment for blood disorders including but not limited to leukemia, lymphoma and sickle cell anemia. The limitation to blood stem cell donation is that the donor and recipient must be a genetic match to ensure the patient's body does not reject the donation. Due to wide genetic diversity, it is extremely difficult for searching patients to find a genetic match, but with every new member of the registry, a patient's chance increases. Our tabling is focused on both education and recruitment for the stony brook university community!

events.title: Who Said Music Ain't Gothic?: Sexual Transgression and Gothic Existence in Beyoncé's Lemonade
events.description:
How does Black life reflect the gothic, and how is that revealed in Black cultural production? Traditionally, the gothic has been defined as a meta genre that is imbued with haunting, possession, sexual transgression, and ruinous landscapes that induce a reckoning with the past. However, I define the gothic as an aesthetic register that’s productive for thinking through the feelings and experiences of Black life. In this talk, I explore how the visual album Lemonade (2016) visually and sonically invokes the gothic genre’s atmosphere and aesthetics to locate the intrinsic conditions of Black unfreedom. We will explore how Lemonade functions as a sexually and racially transgressive text that speaks back and against racialized and gendered violence on Black bodies and their strivings toward freedom. This talk argues that Lemonade operates as a visual grammar for what I term as gothic existence, the idea that Black life is an inherently gothic experience.

events.title: Ropey vs. Rough: The Difference Between Pahoehoe and ʻAʻā Lava Flow Morphologies
events.description:
Did you know lava is named after how it feels to walk on it?! Dive into basaltic lava flow morphology with us, where we'll discuss the difference between the smooth, ropy texture of pahoehoe flows and the rough and sharp ‘a‘ā flows. Afterwards, we'll play a game to see how temperature, viscosity, and even stress can transform the same magma from one flow to the other.

events.title: The Beer Goggles Challenge
events.description:
The Beer Goggles Challenge is an activity designed to simulate the effects of alcohol impairment. Participants wear specially designed goggles that distort vision and coordination, mimicking the sensation of being intoxicated. During the challenge, students attempt simple tasks like walking in a straight line, picking up objects, or navigating obstacles. The goal is to demonstrate how alcohol impairs judgment, reaction time, and motor skills, reinforcing the dangers of driving under the influence or engaging in risky behaviors while intoxicated. It provides a hands-on, impactful learning experience about the real-world consequences of alcohol impairment.

events.title: SIS: Write it Right
events.description:
Write It Right: The Essay Workshop is an educational event hosted by Sigma Iota Sigma designed to help students improve their academic writing skills. The event will feature a presentation covering the essential steps of writing a successful essay, including understanding essay prompts, developing a strong thesis statement, organizing an introduction and body paragraphs, writing an effective conclusion, and properly citing sources. The presentation will provide helpful tips and examples to make essay writing easier to understand and approach. Following the presentation, participants will have the opportunity to engage in interactive activities where they can practice creating thesis statements, organizing essay outlines, and improving sample paragraphs. This event aims to create a supportive learning environment where students can ask questions, share ideas, and gain confidence in their writing abilities. By the end of the workshop, participants will have practical strategies and resources they can apply to future college assignments.
